faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: Everything you need to know about running MediaForge as your local macOS video converter and FFmpeg GUI.

items.q: Do I need to install FFmpeg via Homebrew first?
items.a: The community (open-source) edition expects a system FFmpeg—Homebrew is the easiest path on macOS. App Store / store builds ship with a bundled non-GPL FFmpeg, so no separate install is required.

items.q: Does MediaForge support Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) hardware acceleration?
items.a: Yes. MediaForge runs natively on Apple Silicon and can use VideoToolbox hardware acceleration when available.

items.q: Is MediaForge completely free and open source?
items.a: The MediaForge Open edition on GitHub is free and open source. MediaForge Pro adds paid features such as AI Forge and advanced codecs.

items.q: How do I use FFmpeg on Mac without the terminal?
items.a: Install MediaForge, drop a media file, and choose a visual preset—Quick Export, Make GIF, Extract Audio, image compress, or WebP convert. MediaForge runs FFmpeg for you locally.

items.q: Is MediaForge a free open-source alternative to ffWorks or Permute?
items.a: Yes—MediaForge Open is a free, open-source FFmpeg GUI for macOS focused on local presets for video, GIF, audio, and images. Paid GUIs like ffWorks or Permute offer polished suites; MediaForge prioritizes open core and local-first workflows.

items.q: How does MediaForge compare to HandBrake and Shutter Encoder?
items.a: HandBrake and Shutter Encoder excel at video transcoding. MediaForge is an FFmpeg GUI that also targets high-quality GIF, lossless audio extraction, and WebP/image batch jobs in one local macOS app.
